text:
incident-bot: alert triggered: service_slo_burn > 0.8 over 5m (auto-page) :rotating_light:
Amelia J: seeing this in the dashboard, looks like a short spike in token generation latency, not full outage. paging now — @SRE Oncall can you triage?
SRE Oncall: on it, joining live. grabbing initial traces.
Jason K: heads up — this woke up a few product teams, likely from a retry storm coming from a canary rollout. I pushed a temporary rate limit at the edge ~2m ago.
Priya R: confirm rate-limit was applied? I still see injection of ~3k reqs/min on the tail.
Jason K: yes, applied on canary group via /deploy toggle, rollback queued if it keeps up.
SRE Oncall: quick status: CPU/latency spike on inference pods, error rate still <1% but tail latency causing SLO burn alert. Customer impact: higher end-user latency for a subset of sessions, no 5xx visible.
Amelia J: ok, this is more SLO burn than outage. Can we suppress paging for short bursts while we contain? Recommend switching alert to multi-window smoothing for the next 15m and suppress pages for transient bursts <10m.
Priya R: agreed. Proposal: change the alert to use three-window weighted average: 2m, 10m, 60m with weights 0.6/0.3/0.1. Trigger paging only if weighted >= 0.8 and absolute 60m >= 0.5. That avoids noisy pages for brief canary blips.
Jason K: +1. Also add a "burst-ignore-window" tag so our oncall tooling won't page for single-window spikes originating from canary group.
SRE Oncall: implementing change now. Patch to alert rule coming:```yaml
- alert: SLOHighBurn
  expr: |
    weighted_avg = (0.6 * burn[2m] + 0.3 * burn[10m] + 0.1 * burn[60m])
    weighted_avg > 0.8 and avg_over_time(burn[60m]) > 0.5
  annotations:
    runbook: https://dash.redwood.ai/runbooks/slo-burn
    suppress_tag: burst-ignore
  for: 2m
```
Amelia J: nice, add an annotation that pages should only go to "sre-primary" after 2m sustained and escalate to oncall-lead at 10m.
Priya R: also create a short-term dashboard panel showing the three windows and the weighted score side-by-side so triage can eyeball it quickly. Link it into the alert annotation.
SRE Oncall: done — dashboard panel created: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/slo/escalation-smoothing?panel=3 (temporary view).
incident-bot: rule updated in staging, will roll to prod after CI checks :white_check_mark:
Jason K: while rolling, we should tag the current incident as "canary-induced" and memo for follow-up: needs refinement in deployment gating and autoscale cushion.
Amelia J: logging action items: 1) make alert rule change permanent after 24h observation, 2) add canary backoff in deploy pipeline, 3) increase autoscale headroom for text-gen service, 4) run a replay test to validate smoothing doesn't hide real sustained degradations.
Priya R: I'll open tickets: RDW-4287 (alert smoothing review), RDW-4288 (canary backoff), RDW-4289 (autoscale cushion). Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-sre.
SRE Oncall: paging suppression holding, current weighted score decaying to 0.45 — looks like containment worked. I'll keep monitoring for another 20m then close the incident.
Amelia J: add a temporary mute rule for the canary tag in the incident routing so other services don't cascade pages.
Jason K: FYI I pushed the rollback for the canary flag as backup; leaving it in place until we validate metric behavior.
Priya R: for postmortem, let's capture the alert sensitivity delta: old rule triggered at 2m spikes -> 6 pages in last month; new rule should reduce that by ~70% per our sims. Need to capture false-positive reduction metric.
SRE Oncall: will export sim numbers and attach to RDW-4287.
Amelia J: once this is stable, we should update runbooks to include the "weighted windows" rationale and an example of when to escalate vs monitor.
incident-bot: incident status: mitigated, monitoring. incident_id=INC-2026-0315-003 :eyes:
Jason K: thanks team. :raised_hands: Great coordination.
Priya R: closing loop — I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to review the alert thresholds and the dashboard panels with runtime/product.
SRE Oncall: will handoff to next oncall at 1776543610 — leaving notes in the incident ticket.
Amelia J: ack, handoff received. Marking follow-ups and setting reminder for 24h review. :calendar:
incident-bot: incident closed after 25m of monitoring. :white_check_mark:
